method: stem token Jaccard candidate discovery only; manual stem and all-choice reading required

public.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy receives a microbiology report showing an action-level result, but personnel plan to delay Board notification until final organism identification is complete.

Case B: The same ISO area has another action-level finding within 60 days, separated from the first by an acceptable result.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Any employee may replace the specified reporting role without checking the policy.
An acceptable result between two findings necessarily prevents the described repeat-within-60-days trigger.
The described one-business-day notification clock runs from microbiology-report receipt without waiting for later identification.
Once notification is sent, organism and location trends are no longer relevant.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is asked to give an eligible medication in the pharmacy. Which statements about the permitted route are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: An intravenous infusion is permitted where the pharmacist is trained to place a line.
Any parenteral route is permitted so long as the product label allows it.
The route is at the pharmacist's professional discretion for an eligible product.
Administration must accord with manufacturer approved labeling for the product.
Only subcutaneous or intramuscular injection is permitted.

public.stem:
A pharmacist has completed 20 eligible CE contact hours for the year, including five live clinical hours and a two-hour ACPE-approved home-study course designated as pharmacy law. The law course addresses federal pharmacy requirements, not Massachusetts-specific rules. No specialized-practice requirement applies.

How should the law course be treated for the annual Massachusetts law-CE minimum? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Count it as general CE and add two hours specifically about Massachusetts law.
Count its two hours toward the law minimum as part of the 20-hour total.
Count it as general CE and repeat two law hours in a live format.
Count it toward the law minimum but exclude it from the general 20 hours.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is preparing for renewal. In the first calendar year of the two-year renewal cycle, she completed 24 contact hours. In the second calendar year, she has completed 16 contact hours. Her pharmacy-law and home-study requirements are otherwise satisfied. What is the best way to address the remaining CE requirement?

choices.text: Renew now because the Board looks only at the combined 40-hour total for the two-year cycle.
Complete 4 more contact hours in the second calendar year because the 20-hour minimum applies to each calendar year.
Complete only additional pharmacy-law hours; the annual total no longer matters once the law requirement is met.
Ask the CE provider to redate 4 first-year credits so they count in the second calendar year.
Repeat all 20 second-year hours because completing more than 20 hours in the first year invalidates the surplus-year record.

public.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacist who does not practice CDTM has 9 eligible CE contact hours. The pharmacist then completes 10 eligible hours at a conference on one calendar day. All live, law, and specialized-topic requirements are otherwise satisfied; the question concerns only the 20-hour total.

How many additional eligible contact hours are needed for that calendar year? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: 1 contact hour
11 contact hours
3 contact hours
5 contact hours

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is behind on continuing education for the current calendar year. She attends an intensive live conference held on a single day in December and the authorized provider issues her a statement of credit for 12 contact hours earned that day. She wants to apply all 12 to that calendar year. How many of those contact hours may she apply?

choices.text: The full 12, because the daily restriction applies to home study rather than live programs.
The full 12, because live conference programming carries no daily restriction.
Ten, because a registrant may not exceed ten contact hours in a calendar day.
None, because contact hours earned in December are credited to the following cycle.
Eight, because a registrant may not earn more than eight contact hours in a calendar day.

public.stem:
A pharmacist graduated from an ACPE school in 2021 and first obtains a Massachusetts license by transfer on October 01, 2026. No other CE exception applies.

Under the currently posted CE policy, which deadline applies to the CE required for 2026? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Two years after the license issue date
April 30, 2027
No CE is required for 2026
December 31, 2026

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist entered active armed forces service in November of an even-numbered year and was released from active duty the following spring. Which statement correctly describes the effect on her registration and continuing education?

choices.text: Her registration lapsed on December 31st of that even-numbered year.
Her registration remains valid until 90 days following release from active duty, and the continuing education requirement does not apply to that biennial cycle.
Her registration remains valid indefinitely while she is on active duty and continuing education is merely deferred.
Her registration remains valid for 90 days but the continuing education requirement still applies to that cycle.
Her registration remains valid only if she requested a waiver before deploying.

public.stem:
Case A: A pharmacist has acceptable non-ACPE credits that do not appear in CPE Monitor and discards the course certificates after renewal.

Case B: An instructor teaches the same Board-approved CE program repeatedly in one year and requests a fresh instructor credit for every presentation.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Applicable record-retention rules continue after the renewal transaction.
Evidence should identify the participant, activity, provider, completion, hours, and required credit details.
The stated instructor-credit route allows credit once annually for that program.
Required documentation must be retained for acceptable credits not shown in CPE Monitor.

canonical.stem: Three Massachusetts-licensed pharmacies are closing on the same date: a non-resident Drug Store pharmacy, a resident sterile compounding pharmacy, and an institutional sterile compounding pharmacy. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Each must give the Board certified written notice at least 14 days before closing.
The non-resident pharmacy must make the post-closure submission of original licences.
The sterile compounding pharmacy must identify a pharmacy able to continue patient care.
The institutional sterile compounding pharmacy is excused from the patient-notice duty.
The continuity-of-care pharmacy identified must be licensed by the Board.

public.stem:
An employee has current full technician license but expired national certification. The on-duty pharmacist approves the assignment to handle a new oral Schedule VI prescription; all other routine training is complete.

How should the pharmacist evaluate this assignment? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Restore the state license before assigning licensed technician work.
The identified pharmacist-only boundary still applies.
The assignment is within the stated personnel pathway.
Reassign the task because the stated technician tier does not authorize it.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician trainee working under the direct supervision of a pharmacist is asked to answer the pharmacy telephone during a staffing crunch and take a new prescription from a prescriber's agent. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: The trainee may take the prescription while under direct supervision.
The trainee may take the prescription if the pharmacist listens on a second handset.
The trainee may take the prescription if it is for a Schedule VI drug.
The trainee may not take prescriptions over the telephone.
The trainee may take the prescription after 500 hours of trainee employment.

public.stem:
A prescriber’s agent calls to authorize another refill of an existing Schedule VI prescription. The drug, strength, directions, and other prescription information are unchanged. A licensed noncertified technician and a licensed technician trainee are available; the pharmacist on duty can approve the assignment.

Who may receive this unchanged refill authorization under the stated personnel rules? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The licensed technician, with the pharmacist’s approval for the assignment.
The trainee, if the pharmacist directly supervises the telephone conversation.
Either employee, because the pharmacist will verify the product before dispensing.
Neither employee; a pharmacist must personally receive every unchanged refill authorization.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician telephones a prescriber's office for refill authorization. The office authorizes the refill but also increases the daily dose. The pharmacist on duty had approved the technician making refill calls. What should happen next?

choices.text: The technician may accept the change because the pharmacist pre-approved the call.
The technician may accept the change if she reads it back to the prescriber's agent.
The technician may accept the change and flag it for the pharmacist's final verification.
The technician may accept the change only if she is a certified pharmacy technician.
The technician may not accept the change because information has changed from the previous prescription.

public.stem:
Case A: An 18-year-old applicant passes a listed national technician examination and assumes that no Massachusetts licensing application is needed.

Case B: A pharmacy uses the employer-training pathway after 500 trainee-employment hours and plans a 20-question competency examination.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The employer pathway requires the specified trainee employment before its examination route.
A qualifying national examination supports a licensing pathway but does not itself issue the Board license.
The specified employer competency examination requires at least 50 questions and a 75% passing standard.
The technician-examination percentage is not an MPJE raw-score passing formula.

canonical.stem: A pharmacy technician trainee at an eligible Massachusetts hospital is transporting pharmacist-verified stock into an ADD with required electronic validation. Which drugs fall within the trainee's Schedule III-VI stocking boundary? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Alprazolam
Pregabalin
Gabapentin
Warfarin
Methylphenidate

public.stem:
An employee has a current intern license under direct pharmacist supervision. The on-duty pharmacist approves the assignment to handle final patient-specific prescription verification; all other routine training is complete.

How should the pharmacist evaluate this assignment? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The identified pharmacist-only boundary still applies.
Restore the state license before assigning licensed technician work.
Reassign the task because the stated technician tier does not authorize it.
The assignment is within the stated personnel pathway.

canonical.stem: A Dayvigo prescription is three months old and has two completed refills. Which federal limits must the pharmacist check before the next refill?

choices.text: Check only whether five refills have been completed.
Check only whether six months have elapsed.
Check both the five-refill cap and the six-month issue-date deadline.
Require renewal now because two prior refills exhaust the limit.
Use a one-year window because Dayvigo is prescribed for sleep.

public.stem:
A pharmacy intern has completed the required immunization course and has current CPR certification. The only pharmacist on duty has an active pharmacist license but an expired CPR certificate. A qualified immunizing MOR is away from the pharmacy and offers approval by telephone. The intern is assigned to administer an adult's routine vaccine.

What should the pharmacist on duty do about the intern's assignment? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Defer the assignment until a pharmacist meeting the immunizer requirements can provide direct supervision.
Approve the assignment because an active pharmacist license is sufficient for vaccination supervision.
Approve the assignment because the off-site MOR's telephone authorization supplies direct supervision.
Approve the assignment because CPR currency applies only to the person holding the syringe.

canonical.stem: Assume each prescription is otherwise valid and the pharmacist has completed all required training. Which Massachusetts pharmacist-administration scenarios fall within a current authorized category? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Administer patient-specific Vivitrol for substance use disorder under the applicable prescriber-directed guidance
Administer patient-specific Abilify Maintena for mental illness under the applicable guidance
Administer testosterone cypionate for routine hypogonadism solely because the same product is authorized for gender-affirming care
Administer insulin glargine for diabetes solely because it is a prescription Schedule VI product
Administer prescribed testosterone cypionate for gender-affirming care

public.stem:
NABP approved a pharmacist’s Massachusetts reciprocity application on January 6, 2025. The Board has not issued a license. The applicant uploaded a missing internship document in December 2025 and contacts the Board on February 2, 2026, expecting that upload to have restarted the application period.

How should the pharmacist treat the old application’s validity? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: It remains valid through December 2026, one year after the missing document was uploaded.
It remains valid until the next even-year pharmacist renewal deadline.
It has passed the one-year validity period measured from NABP approval.
It stays valid while the Board is waiting for a final licensing decision.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist teaches the same Board-approved continuing education program four times in one year and separately completes two courses in a postgraduate pharmacy curriculum. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: As a Board-approved instructor she receives credit for the program taught on a one-time basis annually.
She receives separate instructor credit for each of the four presentations.
Postgraduate credit is available only for courses in pharmacy law.
Postgraduate course credit requires the sponsor or co-sponsor to be Board-authorized or ACPE-accredited.
Postgraduate credit requires the course to instruct in pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, pharmacy practice or pharmacy law.

public.stem:
A Massachusetts methylphenidate prescription was issued 34 days ago. It authorizes a 90-day supply, has never been filled, and is presented for routine outpatient dispensing today.

Which fact prevents dispensing under this prescription? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A 90-day supply of a non-opioid CII is categorically prohibited.
The prescription has passed the Massachusetts 30-day validity period.
Methylphenidate prescriptions are limited to a seven-day supply in every adult.
A previously unfilled CII prescription needs a refill authorization.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist's personal registration expired 61 days ago. It has never been suspended or revoked. The pharmacist pays the renewal and late fees this morning and asks to begin a shift while the Board processes the renewal. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: The pharmacist falls within the 60-day fee-only branch and may practice once payment is submitted.
Any lapse beyond 60 days automatically requires passage of the MPJE before renewal.
Direct oversight by another pharmacist permits practice until the registration is renewed.
Board conditions may apply, but the over-two-year MPJE branch does not; practice must wait for renewal.
The registration remains effective for six months after expiration if all continuing education was completed on time.

public.stem:
Case A: A pharmacist manages both a personal Massachusetts pharmacist registration and a Drug Store Pharmacy license and tries to renew both on the same two-year schedule.

Case B: A pharmacy also holds sterile-compounding authorization. Its manager is preparing a calendar for the different renewals.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Drug Store Pharmacy licenses use the pharmacist's birthday renewal cycle.
The personal pharmacist registration follows the odd-numbered-year December 31 cycle.
Renewing the personal pharmacist license also renews the facility licenses.
The specified compounding pharmacy licenses have annual December 31 renewal cycles.

canonical.stem: Three Massachusetts-licensed pharmacies are closing on the same date: a non-resident Drug Store pharmacy, a resident sterile compounding pharmacy, and an institutional sterile compounding pharmacy. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Each must give the Board certified written notice at least 14 days before closing.
The non-resident pharmacy must make the post-closure submission of original licences.
The sterile compounding pharmacy must identify a pharmacy able to continue patient care.
The institutional sterile compounding pharmacy is excused from the patient-notice duty.
The continuity-of-care pharmacy identified must be licensed by the Board.

public.stem:
A physician wants a Massachusetts community pharmacist to issue testosterone prescriptions under a retail CDTM agreement. The patient is an adult and both clinicians meet their qualifications. The proposed agreement explicitly names testosterone.

What is the relevant limitation? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The pharmacist may prescribe it because testosterone is not an opioid.
The pharmacist may prescribe it after adding one extra CE hour.
The community CDTM pathway excludes prescribing of Schedule II–V drugs.
The agreement becomes sufficient if the prescription is limited to 30 days.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has completed no training programme of any kind. She proposes to dispense emergency contraception under the statewide standing order this week, and to dispense a COVID-19 drug under a standing order next week. How do the two proposals compare?

choices.text: The emergency contraception dispensing may proceed; the COVID-19 drug may not.
The COVID-19 dispensing may proceed; the emergency contraception may not.
Both may proceed, because training is a professional expectation rather than a bar.
Neither may proceed, because both regimes require approved training beforehand.
Both may proceed once she notifies the Department that she intends to dispense.

public.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacy creates a rule that treats every PMP-reportable drug as federal Schedule V. It applies that rule to gabapentin and pregabalin.

Which correction is appropriate? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Remove gabapentin from PMP reporting because it is not federally scheduled.
Move pregabalin to Schedule VI because both drugs treat neurologic conditions.
Distinguish federal scheduling from gabapentin's state reporting status.
Apply CII no-refill rules to both because their dispensing is reported.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy's Manager of Record is leaving amicably at the end of the month and a successor has been identified. Which statements about the change of Manager of Record application are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The inventory attestation is signed by both the outgoing and the incoming Manager.
The inventory covers Schedules II through V and reportable Schedule VI substances.
A staff pharmacist may sign in place of the outgoing Manager for convenience.
A certified copy of the Drug Store Pharmacy licence accompanies the application.
The Board may require the proposed Manager of Record to appear before it.

public.stem:
Case A: A licensed pharmacy begins a major configuration change and plans to ask the Board for approval after construction is complete.

Case B: A pharmacy submits a relocation application 90 days before the desired move and treats submission as authorization to relocate immediately.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Submitting a relocation application does not itself constitute Board approval to move.
Applicable remodeling and configuration changes require Board approval before the work starts.
Replacing a sterile-compounding secondary control is exempt merely because the address is unchanged.
The ordinary relocation application timing is at least 90 days before the desired date unless otherwise approved.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is preparing a new prescription for delivery to a patient's home. To satisfy the counseling-offer requirement for off-site delivery, the pharmacy provides access to its toll-free service that connects the patient with a pharmacist. Before the prescription is sent, which additional step is required under Massachusetts law?

choices.text: Print the toll-free service number on a label affixed to each prescription drug container.
Place the number only on the outer shipping package, as long as it remains visible until opening.
Include the number only on the delivery receipt that the patient signs.
Send the number in an electronic message after the package has been delivered.
Replace the toll-free number with the dispensing pharmacy's ordinary local number on the container label.

public.stem:
Case A: A Massachusetts applicant has completed an approved PharmD program but will be 17 on the scheduled examination date. The application is otherwise complete.

Case B: A licensing coordinator compares an ACPE graduate with a graduate of a non-approved foreign pharmacy school before submitting their Massachusetts applications.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The employer's offer establishes the applicant's licensing eligibility.
A foreign-school diploma alone replaces FPGEC certification evidence.
Internship requirements remain a separate part of licensure eligibility.
Graduation waives the minimum age for the examination pathway.

canonical.stem: Three Massachusetts-licensed pharmacies are closing on the same date: a non-resident Drug Store pharmacy, a resident sterile compounding pharmacy, and an institutional sterile compounding pharmacy. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Each must give the Board certified written notice at least 14 days before closing.
The non-resident pharmacy must make the post-closure submission of original licences.
The sterile compounding pharmacy must identify a pharmacy able to continue patient care.
The institutional sterile compounding pharmacy is excused from the patient-notice duty.
The continuity-of-care pharmacy identified must be licensed by the Board.

public.stem:
Case A: Two licensed nationally certified technicians perform a Schedule II perpetual-inventory count under the specified pharmacist verification arrangement.

Case B: One technician finds a discrepancy and edits the balance without involving the MOR or the designated pharmacist.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A certified technician may make permitted perpetual-inventory entries.
Matching the electronic total to the count completes the required discrepancy investigation.
The permitted paired-technician count still requires the supervising pharmacist's verification.
A discrepancy adjustment follows the MOR or authorized pharmacist-designee pathway.

canonical.stem: A provider is preparing two Board approval requests: one for a home-study program and one for a live program. Which statements about the Board's criteria are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A home-study program must contain a test to indicate progress and verify completion.
A home-study program must involve the learner by requiring an active response and providing feedback.
A live program shall involve direct interaction between the faculty and participants.
A live program must also supply a bibliography for continued study as a condition of approval.
Participants shall be given the opportunity to evaluate faculty, learning experiences and facilities.

public.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacist first seeks a CDTM agreement in 2026 after three years of licensed practice. The pharmacist holds current Board of Pharmacy Specialties certification, has completed the practice site's comprehensive credentialing and training, and has current BLS certification. All other CDTM qualifications are satisfied.

How should the pharmacist assess the five-year experience requirement? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Wait for five years of licensed practice because certification cannot satisfy equivalency.
Complete an ASHP PGY2 residency in addition to the current BPS certification.
Use site credentialing alone as the recognized substitute for five years of practice.
Use the current BPS certification and completed site requirements as a recognized equivalency.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has not sought an extension or other relief from the Board. Which continuing education plan satisfies the annual requirements?

choices.text: Five live hours, including one hour of pharmacy law, plus 15 home-study hours with no additional pharmacy-law content
Four live hours, including two hours of pharmacy law, plus 16 home-study hours
Six live hours, including one hour of pharmacy law, plus 14 home-study hours that include one hour of pharmacy law
Nine live hours, including two hours of pharmacy law, plus 10 home-study hours
Three live hours, including two hours of pharmacy law, plus 17 home-study hours

public.stem:
A pharmacist practices under separate diabetes and hypertension CDTM agreements throughout the year. The pharmacist completed the usual 20 eligible CE hours plus four additional Board-approved hours related to those agreements. One of the additional hours is accepted prescribing-related pain-management education. All live, law and other applicable content requirements are satisfied.

What is the minimum additional education needed to reach the CDTM annual-hour requirement? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Six more related hours, because each agreement adds a separate five-hour minimum.
One more related hour, bringing the total to 25 with five beyond the usual 20.
Two more related hours, because pain-management education cannot count toward the additional five.
No more hours, because the four CDTM hours can also be counted a second time in the total.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is preparing for renewal. In the first calendar year of the two-year renewal cycle, she completed 24 contact hours. In the second calendar year, she has completed 16 contact hours. Her pharmacy-law and home-study requirements are otherwise satisfied. What is the best way to address the remaining CE requirement?

choices.text: Renew now because the Board looks only at the combined 40-hour total for the two-year cycle.
Complete 4 more contact hours in the second calendar year because the 20-hour minimum applies to each calendar year.
Complete only additional pharmacy-law hours; the annual total no longer matters once the law requirement is met.
Ask the CE provider to redate 4 first-year credits so they count in the second calendar year.
Repeat all 20 second-year hours because completing more than 20 hours in the first year invalidates the surplus-year record.

public.stem:
Case A: A newly fully licensed technician has 600 hours of trainee employment, no national certification, and no hours worked after full technician licensure.

Case B: Another fully licensed technician has current PTCB certification but has not completed vaccination-specific training.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The national-certification and post-licensure-experience options are alternative qualifying routes.
National certification permits vaccination without the required Massachusetts technician license.
National certification does not eliminate the separate vaccination-training requirements.
Trainee hours alone do not satisfy the alternative requiring 500 hours after full technician licensure.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has completed the required administration training and maintains current CPR certification. Each option involves a medication that appears on the MH/SUD administration list. Which requests may proceed under the current guidance? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A 34-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Vivitrol supplied in its single-dose presentation
A 45-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for Invega Sustenna, but this would be the patient's first dose of the medication
A 39-year-old patient requests Abilify Maintena from anonymous pharmacy floor stock that is not tied to a patient-specific prescribed single dose
A 17-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Invega Sustenna
A 52-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Abilify Maintena supplied as the prescribed single dose

public.stem:
A Massachusetts intern logs 13 hours on one day and 13 hours on a separate day at an otherwise approved training site. Only the internship-credit ceiling is being evaluated; this question does not authorize any otherwise prohibited work schedule.

What is the maximum combined internship credit for the two days? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: 12 hours
26 hours
24 hours
23 hours

canonical.stem: A pharmacy student completes 12 hours of qualifying Massachusetts pharmacy-internship activity in one day. The student then remains at the site for a separate two-hour school seminar, and the preceptor proposes recording all 14 hours as Board internship credit. What should be recorded? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The preceptor should record no more than 12 qualifying internship hours for that day.
No more than 12 hours may be credited toward the pharmacy internship in one day.
The extra seminar may be documented separately as school activity, but it cannot increase that day's Board internship credit.
Combining internship work with separately documented educational activity does not raise the Board's maximum internship credit above 12 hours for that day.
All 14 hours may count as internship credit whenever the preceptor signs both the internship log and the seminar attendance record.

public.stem:
Case A: An out-of-state pharmacy plans to ship Massachusetts prescription medications under its home-state license without obtaining the applicable Massachusetts nonresident authorization.

Case B: Its application includes a good-standing letter issued eight months earlier and an inspection conducted more than three years before submission.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Home-state licensure does not replace the applicable Massachusetts nonresident pharmacy license.
The two PIC roles must be held by the same individual in every nonresident pharmacy.
An eight-month-old good-standing letter and a three-year-old inspection meet the stated freshness benchmarks.
A home-state pharmacist-in-charge automatically satisfies the Massachusetts-designated PIC requirement without MA licensure.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is deciding how to package several daily medications for one patient. Which statements correctly apply the Schedule II/III rule? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A stable maintenance classification permits a Schedule II drug to share a multi-drug single-dose pouch.
A licensee may not dispense a Schedule II or III controlled substance in a multi-drug single-dose package.
That prohibition does not by its own terms ban a single-drug single-dose package.
Every form of compliance packaging is prohibited for every Schedule II or III controlled substance.
The policy phrase 'unless otherwise prohibited' preserves the regulatory Schedule II/III restriction.

public.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacy has reasonable grounds to conclude that a compounded preparation already dispensed may be defective. No patient injury has yet been confirmed, and some of the same preparation remains in the pharmacy.

Which response is appropriate under the stated defect framework? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Wait for a serious adverse event before taking the product out of use.
Document only a supplier return and omit the patient distribution record.
Initiate recall and quarantine without waiting for confirmed patient harm.
Release the remaining preparation until a repeat test confirms the first concern.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist's personal registration expired 61 days ago. It has never been suspended or revoked. The pharmacist pays the renewal and late fees this morning and asks to begin a shift while the Board processes the renewal. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: The pharmacist falls within the 60-day fee-only branch and may practice once payment is submitted.
Any lapse beyond 60 days automatically requires passage of the MPJE before renewal.
Direct oversight by another pharmacist permits practice until the registration is renewed.
Board conditions may apply, but the over-two-year MPJE branch does not; practice must wait for renewal.
The registration remains effective for six months after expiration if all continuing education was completed on time.

public.stem:
An owner tracks a pharmacist registration, a Drug Store Pharmacy license, and a sterile-compounding pharmacy license. None is provisional.

Which calendar entries match the renewal distinctions in the notes? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Odd-numbered-year December 31 for the Drug Store Pharmacy license.
The pharmacist's birthday for all three permissions.
Even-numbered-year December 31 for the personal pharmacist registration.
One facility payment renews every professional registration at that address.
Annual December 31 renewal for the specified sterile-compounding license.

canonical.stem: A ketamine prescription is presented to a Massachusetts community pharmacy. Which statements must be considered? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Ketamine is Schedule II and cannot be refilled.
Massachusetts treats ketamine as Schedule VI.
Schedule III refill limits apply to authorized refills.
Covered outpatient dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.
Its anesthetic indication does not change Schedule III status.

public.stem:
A pharmacist's registration expired 20 days ago without disciplinary action. A renewal payment is pending, and no order authorizes continued practice.

Which action is appropriate for an independently staffed dispensing shift today? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Arrange coverage by a pharmacist with current authority to work this shift.
Work the shift if the renewal receipt is displayed next to the certificate.
Work the shift as a retired pharmacist until renewal is processed.
Work the shift because additional Board conditions begin only after 60 days.

canonical.stem: A California prescriber issued an otherwise valid methylphenidate prescription six days ago. The patient presents it today at a Massachusetts pharmacy. Which threshold issue is dispositive?

choices.text: California is outside the narcotic contiguous-state list.
Methylphenidate becomes Schedule VI when issued outside Massachusetts.
The prescription is eligible because nonnarcotic Schedule II prescriptions have no timing gate.
The Massachusetts five-day presentation window has passed.

public.stem:
Case A: A prescriber issues several separate Schedule II prescriptions on one date and proposes postdating the later prescriptions' issue dates.

Case B: One prescription has an earliest-fill date 60 days after the actual issuance, and staff rely only on the federal multiple-prescription allowance to use it in Massachusetts.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The prescriptions use their actual issue dates, with separate appropriate earliest-fill instructions.
A total of 90 days alone establishes compliance with every condition of the federal pathway.
Federal multiple-prescription permission overrides the Massachusetts validity limit in this scenario.
Multiple separate prescriptions are legally refills of one Schedule II prescription.

canonical.stem: On August 14, a practitioner lawfully issues three separate Schedule II prescriptions intended for sequential fills. How should the later prescriptions be dated and controlled?

choices.text: Date each prescription with the future month in which the patient is expected to fill it.
Use the actual August 14 issue date and place appropriate earliest-fill instructions on the later prescriptions.
Leave the issue date blank until the pharmacy receives each prescription.
Convert the second and third prescriptions into refills on the first prescription.
Have the pharmacy create new prescriptions when each month arrives.

public.stem:
Case A: A Schedule II supply was partially dispensed solely because of pharmacy stock shortage, with no actual patient or prescriber request for the alternative request-based pathway.

Case B: After 72 hours passes, staff relabel the original transaction as patient-requested solely to claim a longer remainder window.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A genuinely authorized request must be documented and evaluated under its own conditions.
The original facts support the shortage pathway rather than an invented patient request.
A retrospective label change does not establish an actual qualifying request that did not occur.
Changing the partial-fill category permits increasing the total quantity beyond the original authorization.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a valid oxycodone Schedule II prescription for 30 tablets but has only 12 tablets in stock. The patient wants the full prescribed quantity; the pharmacy dispenses 12 solely because it cannot supply the rest. Four days later the remaining stock arrives. What is the controlling federal consequence?

choices.text: The balance may be dispensed within 30 days because every Schedule II partial fill uses the patient-requested 30-day pathway.
The pharmacy may treat the remaining 18 tablets as a refill because the original total quantity was not dispensed.
The remaining 18 tablets may be transferred to another pharmacy once the original pharmacy receives stock.
The ordinary 72-hour shortage-remainder period has passed, so further quantity generally requires prescriber notification and a new prescription.
The original pharmacy may dispense the balance at any time before the Massachusetts 30-day Schedule II validity period ends.

public.stem:
Case A: An emergency oral Schedule II prescription is partially filled at the patient's request, and staff apply the ordinary nonemergency 30-day requested-partial window.

Case B: A Massachusetts patient asks a different pharmacy in the same chain to provide a remainder after an initial requested partial fill at the first pharmacy.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Shortage and emergency requested partial use one identical starting event merely because both say 72 hours.
The same chain name makes every location the same pharmacy for the requested remainder.
Any remaining quantity counts as an initially unfilled EPCS eligible for initial transfer.
The federal emergency-oral requested-partial remainder limit is 72 hours from issuance rather than the ordinary 30-day period.

canonical.stem: A clonazepam Schedule IV prescription is written for 90 tablets. The patient asks to receive 30 tablets today and the rest in later partial dispensings. Which statements describe the federal partial-fill framework? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Each partial dispensing is recorded in the same manner as a refill.
The first 30-tablet partial dispensing automatically cancels all authority to dispense the remaining quantity.
The total quantity dispensed through all partial fills may not exceed the quantity prescribed.
The partial-dispensing sequence must remain within the applicable six-month federal prescription period.
The patient may extend the partial-dispensing period indefinitely by requesting smaller quantities each month.

public.stem:
An employee has current full technician license and current national certification. The on-duty pharmacist approves the assignment to handle an emergency oral Schedule II authorization; all other routine training is complete.

How should the pharmacist evaluate this assignment? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Reassign the task because the stated technician tier does not authorize it.
The assignment is within the stated personnel pathway.
Restore the state license before assigning licensed technician work.
The identified pharmacist-only boundary still applies.

canonical.stem: A pharmacist lawfully dispensed a three-day emergency oral Schedule II prescription after speaking directly with the prescriber. Eight days later, the pharmacy still has not received the required follow-up prescription despite documented requests to the prescriber. What federal step now becomes important for the pharmacist?

choices.text: Convert the emergency dispensing into a Schedule III refill so the existing record can remain open.
Delete the emergency prescription record because the prescriber failed to complete the follow-up.
Wait until 30 days after the oral authorization because the prescriber still has the full Schedule II validity period.
Reverse the original dispensing claim and treat the medication as an undocumented sample.
Notify DEA of the prescriber's failure to deliver the required emergency follow-up prescription.

public.stem:
Case A: During a qualifying temporary power failure, an otherwise valid paper prescription is issued under an applicable electronic-prescribing exception.

Case B: A prescriber with an electronic-prescribing waiver proposes an ordinary oral Schedule II refill without satisfying an emergency pathway.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: An LTCF exception with a past endpoint remains universally available without a verified extension.
The waiver does not create an ordinary oral Schedule II refill authority.
The pharmacist's specific exception-verification relief does not waive authenticity or prescriber-authority review.
A paper prescription is necessarily invalid even when an applicable electronic-prescribing exception exists.

canonical.stem: Each scenario involves methadone. Which statements correctly reflect how indication changes the federal pharmacy pathway? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Methadone remains Schedule II whether it is used for pain or for opioid-use-disorder treatment.
A pain prescription automatically becomes invalid if the patient also has a history of OUD
A valid methadone prescription for pain can be evaluated under ordinary Schedule II prescription rules, subject to applicable state law
An ordinary community-pharmacy prescription written solely for ongoing OUD maintenance cannot be treated as routine Schedule II pain prescribing outside the applicable narcotic-treatment pathway
A qualifying non-OTP emergency provision is a narrow dispense-only bridge while referral is arranged

public.stem:
Case A: A valid Schedule II prescription is faxed for a resident of a qualifying long-term-care facility.

Case B: A separate hospice fax concerns a Schedule II nonnarcotic drug, and staff invoke the hospice-narcotic exception without considering whether another lawful pathway applies.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The described federal LTCF fax-as-original route is not limited to narcotic Schedule II drugs.
Any informal description of comfort care necessarily establishes the qualifying hospice fax pathway.
The hospice-narcotic exception itself covers every Schedule II drug regardless of narcotic status.
Fax-as-original status removes all other prescription requirements.

canonical.stem: A pharmacy serving a long-term-care facility receives a faxed Schedule II prescription for an LTCF resident. The prescription is otherwise valid. Which federal rule is most relevant to whether the fax may serve as the original?

choices.text: The fax can serve as the original for the Schedule II prescription to the LTCF resident under the specific federal exception.
The exception applies only if the Schedule II drug is a narcotic.
The fax is never an original because LTCF status affects only partial filling.
The fax becomes valid only after seven days have elapsed.
The facility must convert the prescription to Schedule III before the fax can be used.

public.stem:
Case A: A certified technician is asked, with pharmacist approval, to transfer remaining authorized refills of a Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription.

Case B: The same employee is asked to transfer a Schedule IV refill between two independent pharmacies and assumes the Schedule VI personnel rule also applies.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The federal controlled-refill transfer requires the licensed-pharmacist communication pathway.
A technician-performed VI transfer creates a fresh year of validity.
The specified certified-technician transfer authority is for Schedule VI prescriptions.
The patient's timely-transfer right does not expand the worker's professional scope.

canonical.stem: A patient requests a permissible transfer of an unfilled electronic Sonata prescription that includes two authorized refills to another DEA-registered retail pharmacy. The sending pharmacist asks whether only the initial fill can move while the two refills remain at the original pharmacy. What is the correct federal result?

choices.text: Only the initial fill transfers; the authorized refills must remain at the original pharmacy.
The initial fill transfers now, and each authorized refill may later be transferred separately.
The authorized refills transfer with the original prescription, so the entire prescription moves to the receiving pharmacy.
The receiving pharmacy must cancel both refills because controlled-substance refills cannot transfer electronically.
The patient may divide the refills between both pharmacies if the two pharmacists agree.

public.stem:
Case A: At the patient's request, two DEA-registered retail pharmacies arrange an eligible initial transfer of a never-dispensed electronic Schedule II prescription where state law permits it.

Case B: To accomplish the transfer, staff print the prescription and fax the printout while changing part of its signed content.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Associated III-V refills must remain separately active at the originating pharmacy.
Only the recipient keeps initial-transfer records, beginning at a future last refill.
Printing, faxing, and changing signed content preserve the required electronic-transfer form.
The described initial unfilled EPCS pathway is possible on a one-time basis under its conditions.

canonical.stem: At the patient's request, one DEA-registered retail pharmacy is asked to transfer an unfilled electronic MS Contin prescription to another DEA-registered retail pharmacy. Which pathway applies?

choices.text: Print the electronic prescription and fax the image.
Transfer it repeatedly while no quantity has been dispensed.
Have technicians at both pharmacies complete the transfer without pharmacist communication.
Use a one-time pharmacist-to-pharmacist electronic transfer after confirming state permission and federal compliance.
Treat the transaction as a Schedule II refill at the receiving pharmacy.

public.stem:
A certified technician routinely performs pharmacist-approved Schedule VI prescription transfers. A pharmacist at another pharmacy now calls for the remaining refills of a previously filled Schedule IV prescription. The pharmacies do not share a real-time database, and the prescription is otherwise eligible for its first refill transfer.

How should the pharmacy handle this transfer call? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Let the technician complete the call and have the pharmacist sign the transfer record afterward.
Let the technician transfer the refills because the original prescription has already been dispensed.
Let the technician transfer it after confirming active DEA registrations for both pharmacies.
Connect the receiving pharmacist with the pharmacist on duty to complete the transfer.

canonical.stem: A hospice patient needs a Schedule II narcotic. The prescriber faxes a valid prescription to the pharmacy and clearly indicates on the prescription that the patient is a hospice patient. What is the federal consequence of those facts?

choices.text: The fax may serve as the original Schedule II prescription under the hospice narcotic exception.
The fax is an original only if the patient also resides in an LTCF.
Hospice status permits refills on the Schedule II prescription.
The pharmacy must wait for a paper original before dispensing in every hospice case.
The notation is irrelevant because hospice exceptions apply only to Schedule III-V drugs.

public.stem:
Case A: An emergency oral Schedule II prescription is partially filled at the patient's request, and staff apply the ordinary nonemergency 30-day requested-partial window.

Case B: A Massachusetts patient asks a different pharmacy in the same chain to provide a remainder after an initial requested partial fill at the first pharmacy.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The federal emergency-oral requested-partial remainder limit is 72 hours from issuance rather than the ordinary 30-day period.
Shortage and emergency requested partial use one identical starting event merely because both say 72 hours.
The described Massachusetts requested-remainder pathway requires the same dispensing pharmacy.
A partly dispensed Schedule II order is not an initially unfilled EPCS for the one-time initial-transfer pathway.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is deciding how to package several daily medications for one patient. Which statements correctly apply the Schedule II/III rule? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A stable maintenance classification permits a Schedule II drug to share a multi-drug single-dose pouch.
A licensee may not dispense a Schedule II or III controlled substance in a multi-drug single-dose package.
That prohibition does not by its own terms ban a single-drug single-dose package.
Every form of compliance packaging is prohibited for every Schedule II or III controlled substance.
The policy phrase 'unless otherwise prohibited' preserves the regulatory Schedule II/III restriction.

public.stem:
Case A: A Schedule III prescription is first filled several months after issuance, and staff start the six-month refill clock on that first-fill date.

Case B: After a lawful transfer, the receiving pharmacy proposes another fresh six-month period beginning with transfer.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Transfer renews the prescription for six additional months.
Unused refills can be dispensed after expiration simply because some remain.
Writing 'PRN' removes the six-month and refill-count limits.
The stated refill window runs from the original issue date.

canonical.stem: The profile shows a phentermine prescription issued four months earlier; four refills have been dispensed and one remains. Which conclusions govern the next fill? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The remaining refill may be dispensed before the six-month deadline.
The dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.
The prescription remains refillable for one year.
Phentermine is Schedule II and cannot be refilled.
Weight-loss drugs are excluded from MassPAT.

public.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacist reviews methylphenidate for a valid indication. The prescriber has authorized at least 90 days, the prescription is otherwise in date, and no separate patient-specific or product limit is more restrictive. Evaluate the statutory single-fill ceiling, not whether the pharmacy should supply that entire amount.

Under Policy 2024-05 and c.94C §23(d), what is the applicable maximum days-supply category? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: 60 days
90 days
7 days
30 days

canonical.stem: A methylphenidate Schedule II prescription is issued for an LTCF resident and the pharmacy will partially fill it over time under the federal special pathway. What maximum time framework applies from the prescription's issue date, unless it is discontinued sooner?

choices.text: A 72-hour partial-fill window
A 7-day partial-fill window
A 90-day partial-fill window
A 60-day period measured from the prescription issue date
A 6-month partial-fill window

public.stem:
A Schedule IV prescription is two months old and authorizes one refill. The initial fill and that refill have both been dispensed.

What is required before dispensing another ordinary refill? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Change the issue date to the latest dispensing date.
Transfer the prescription to create a new refill allowance.
Obtain proper additional authorization or a new prescription.
Use four more refills because the legal maximum is five.

canonical.stem: A valid Massachusetts doxycycline prescription for a chlamydia partner uses 'EPT' in place of the partner's name and address. The pharmacist will dispense it. Which record setup is appropriate?

choices.text: Create a separate profile and prescription label using the EPT designation in place of the partner name/address.
Place the partner's doxycycline under the index patient's profile as an extra refill.
Dispense the drug with no profile or label because the partner is unnamed.
Invent a partner date of birth and legal name to make the software accept the prescription.
Convert doxycycline to OTC status for this transaction.

public.stem:
Case A: The pharmacy's internal record has correct directions, but the patient container label omits them.

Case B: Staff insist every field required on the original prescription, including the prescriber's DEA number, must automatically be printed on every patient label.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A correct internal record does not cure missing required information on the patient label.
Every original-prescription field is necessarily required on the patient container label.
Attaching a technician-prepared label transfers final validation responsibility to the technician.
A drug-class name necessarily identifies every strength and dosage form on a patient label.

canonical.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is filling a written prescription for a controlled substance dispensed as capsules. Which items must appear on the label the pharmacist affixes to the container? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The prescribing practitioner's registration number.
The filling pharmacist's initials.
The serial number of the prescription.
The number of capsules in the container.
The date of filling, and the pharmacy name and address.
